claims.text: Adding phonon-dispersion and chemical-fluctuation descriptors to an ML model will improve prediction accuracy for low lattice thermal conductivity in HEAs relative to models lacking those descriptors.
FeCoCrMnNi is a disordered, multi-principal-element HEA.
Representative HEAs such as FeCoCrMnNi have been synthesized and experimentally characterized.
Binary-alloy datasets can be used to train an ML model for predicting low lattice thermal conductivity in HEAs.
Predictions and validations will be performed from room temperature to moderately high temperatures.
Phonon scattering dominates thermal transport under the intended application and validation conditions.
Acoustic phonon dispersion and force-constant or chemical-fluctuation metrics are associated with phonon scattering and lattice thermal conductivity.
Force-constant fluctuations in FeCoCrMnNi are approximately 20%.
Force-constant fluctuations scatter acoustic phonons in FeCoCrMnNi.
The phonon dynamics and attenuation in FeCoCrMnNi resemble those in corresponding binary alloys.
Lattice distortion in HEAs can reduce phonon velocity and enhance phonon scattering, resulting in low lattice thermal conductivity.
Binary-derived physics descriptors can capture the full disorder-related scattering behavior needed for more accurate HEA predictions.
The physics-informed model will have lower lattice-thermal-conductivity prediction error than a conventional ML model.
The physics-informed model will identify HEA compositions with significantly lower lattice thermal conductivity.
Conventional ML models or empirical rules without the proposed descriptors may misestimate disorder-induced phonon scattering.
The approach will work best when HEA elements and interactions are analogous to those represented in the binary training data.
Performance may degrade for elements or interactions substantially outside the binary training-data domain.
Binary alloys and FeCoCrMnNi exhibit similar phonon-scattering behavior and comparable force-constant fluctuations.
A failure to achieve more than a 10% statistically significant reduction in prediction error across multiple HEA samples would falsify the hypothesis.
Observed phonon-scattering behavior incompatible with the model-assigned descriptors would falsify the proposed mechanism.
